paragraphs: Here's what this whole passage says, friend: the Lord opens hearts, and He doesn't care who is holding the door. A businesswoman by the river hears Paul, and "The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message." (Acts 16:14) Then a jailer who is about to end his own life asks, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?" (Acts 16:30) Two people who could not be more different, one story, and the same Lord doing the opening.

And look at the answer they get. "Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, you and your household." (Acts 16:31) Nobody hands the jailer a to-do list or tells him to earn it. Salvation was never a cookie you bake your way into, friend, it's a gift, and in this story his whole household was baptized and REJOICING "that they had come to believe in God." (Acts 16:34)

Now check out Paul and Silas, because I think this is where it gets personal for you. They were beaten and locked in the inner cell, and at midnight they were "praying and singing hymns to God," while the other prisoners listened. (Acts 16:25) I think their midnight was not the end of the story, friend, because the story goes on to an earthquake and a jailer asking how to be saved. So when your night gets long, baker, keep praying, keep singing, and keep believing, because the Lord opened a heart by the river, and in that prison the doors flew open too.
